Powerlifting Watch: Probably the most comprehensive powerlifting hub. Information on meets, meet results, international rankings, world records &c.

NSFW Chaos and Pain: Jamie Lewis, former recordholder and porn enthusiast, posts about training, stuff he likes, metal, &c. While Jamie's style can be quite abrasive, and even with images removed his blog is pretty NSFW, he offers very interesting and refreshing voice about training. Probably best known for popularizing behind-the-neck snatch grip press (Klokov Press) and behind-the-neck "push jerks," Jamie generally espouses extreme volume, high-risk, high-reward training. He frequently writes biographies of powerlifters and strongmen and hundreds of interesting routines can be found on his site.

The Tight Tan Slacks of Deszo Ban: Despite lacking in NSFW content and editorializing, this site filled the void for me after I read the entire C&P archive. There are so many primary sources here, lots of excellent and not-so-excellent writing about strength sports and bygone physical culture. Highly recommended.

Reddit: Where mdisbrow gets ceaselessly dickrode, and the answer to every question is "compete more" or "do 5/3/1"

T-Nation/Biotest: Although generally comparable to the back issues of the magazines you see while waiting for the dentist, T-Nation occasionally has a decent or interesting piece by someone famous, if not someone competent.

Supertraining Podcast with Mark Bell: I used to listen to this when I worked nights. It's OK?

Alexander Kang: Sort of a controversial figure in strength circles because of his abrasiveness, his channel has some excellent form tutorials, and unlike most youtubers, he actually makes allowances for different morphology.

Jacko Gill: This is the kid who beat NBA centre Steven Adams at the shotput. His training videos are super varied and interesting, although will probably serve more as a curiosity than actual inspiration for any alterations to your existing regime.

Bigger Faster Stronger: Probably a quasi-illegal upload, but it's on Netflix, or at least was, last I checked. Anyway, this movie is by Mark Bell's brother Chris, and it's an excellent documentary about performance enhancing drugs, strength sports and wrestling culture, and masculinity in American culture. I can't do it justice, so I won't try to describe it anymore.

Raw Iron: Arnold's later commentary about Pumping Iron, the classic documentary about the 1977 Olympia.

Strongman: Hugo Girard: A documentary about my childhood hero, WSM competitor Hugo Girard.

VICE: The Giants of Iceland: What it sounds like, a 20-minute VICE documentary about Icelandic strongmen and the legacies of Jon Pall Sigmarsson and Magnus Ver Magnusson.

Black Iron Beast: If you know what you're doing, you can make a pretty decent 5/3/1 variation with this site.
